 Popular Blood Pressure Medication Recalled Nationwide Over Potential Metal Contamination 
 Popular Blood Pressure Medication Recalled Nationwide Over Potential Metal Contamination 
 Here’s how to check if your meds are affected.
 By Jenn Gonick Published: Nov 17, 2026 10:20 AM EST Save Article Share Article Grace Cary // Getty Images 2 min read Key Points 
 One lot of a popular blood pressure medication has been recalled nationwide by Breckenridge Pharmaceutical, Inc.
 The recalled capsules may be contaminated with metal.
 Here’s how to tell if your meds are affected.
 If you have high blood pressure and rely on a prescription medication to manage it, you may want to take a second look at the label before popping your next pill: A popular blood pressure medication has been recalled nationwide.
 The voluntary recall was initiated on November 16 by Breckenridge Pharmaceutical, Inc., due to potential metal contamination of the affected meds. Per the firm’s announcement , “use of product from the affected lot could potentially cause lacerations of soft tissues in the oral cavity, esophagus, stomach, or intestine.” The recall is “being conducted with the knowledge of the U.S. Food and Drug Administration,” though the FDA has yet to issue a press release.
 Here’s everything you need to know.
 Which products are affected by the recall?
 The recall includes one lot of Propranolol Hydrochloride Extended-Release Capsules, which were manufactured by Adare Pharma Solutions and distributed to wholesalers and pharmacies nationwide between October 26, 2026, and November 4, 2026. Check your medicine cabinet for the following:
 Add Prevention as a preferred source in your Google search results. Use your Google account to add this to your settings. Add to Google settings Propranolol Hydrochloride Extended-Release Capsules, USP, 60 mg 
 Package size: 100-count bottle
 NDC: 51991-817-01
 Lot number: PK25110035
 Expiration date: May 2029
 More information, including photos of the capsules and their packaging, can be found in the announcement from Breckenridge Pharmaceutical .
 What should you do with a recalled product?
 As of right now, Breckenridge hasn’t reported any illnesses or injuries associated with the recall. However, if you do have the recalled meds in your home, the firm says you should immediately stop taking them and contact your doctor for medical advice and replacement instructions. You can return any unused meds included in the recall to the pharmacy where you originally got them.
 If you have questions about the recall, you can contact Breckenridge at 1-855-736-0807 or recall@qualanex.com during regular business hours. If you’ve already taken the recalled meds and have any health concerns, call your doctor right away.
